name: San Antonio Spurs
notes: The Spurs play in the Western Conference's Southwest Division, hosting games at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. The franchise is in the Victor Wembanyama era: after a post-Kawhi/Duncan rebuild, Wembanyama anchored a 62-20 team that reached the 2025-26 NBA Finals and won him a unanimous Defensive Player of the Year award. The roster returned largely intact for 2026-27, adding veteran forward Tobias Harris in free agency.

roster.facts: 2025-26 Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA First Team center who led the Spurs to the 2026 NBA Finals.
roster.name: Victor Wembanyama

roster.facts: Signed a four-year, $229 million extension in 2026 after averaging 18.6 points and leading San Antonio's run to the NBA Finals.
roster.name: De'Aaron Fox

roster.facts: Back-to-back Spurs Rookie of the Year (2025), now entering year three as Wembanyama's co-star backcourt partner and franchise building block.
roster.name: Stephon Castle

roster.facts: No. 2 overall pick in 2025 who made the All-Rookie First Team and starred in the Western Conference Finals as a rookie.
roster.name: Dylan Harper

roster.facts: Starting shooting guard and double-digit scorer whose 2025-26 season was repeatedly interrupted by adductor, hamstring, and rib injuries.
roster.name: Devin Vassell

roster.facts: Rewarded with a three-year, $45 million deal in June 2026 after starting 68 games and leading the Spurs in three-point percentage.
roster.name: Julian Champagnie

roster.facts: 34-year-old veteran leader who took an $11 million pay cut to re-sign in 2026, mentoring San Antonio's young core after the Finals run.
roster.name: Harrison Barnes

roster.facts: Signed a two-year, $31 million deal in July 2026, bringing veteran scoring depth off the bench after two playoff runs in Detroit.
roster.name: Tobias Harris

roster.facts: Shifted into a sixth-man role in 2025-26 and drew trade interest, though he remains on a team-friendly deal through 2026-27.
roster.name: Keldon Johnson

roster.facts: Signed a four-year, $41 million deal in 2025 to back up Wembanyama at center, fresh off a title run with Boston.
roster.name: Luke Kornet

roster.facts: 2025 first-round pick (No. 14) who flashed two-way wing upside as a rookie and is tabbed to climb the depth chart.
roster.name: Carter Bryant

roster.facts: No. 20 pick in the 2026 draft whose stock fell after a torn ACL; he's expected to miss most of his rookie season recovering.
roster.name: Jayden Quaintance

roster.facts: Drafted 26th in 2026 by Denver and immediately traded to San Antonio, the UConn big man enters as a rookie depth piece.
roster.name: Tarris Reed Jr.

roster.facts: Two-way forward who earned G League Player of the Week in February 2026, averaging 22.2 points and 13.4 rebounds for Austin.
roster.name: Harrison Ingram

roster.facts: Re-signed to his third straight two-way deal in 2026 after averaging 26.2 points in the G League, though coming off ankle surgery.
roster.name: David Jones Garcia

roster.facts: Undrafted wing signed to a two-way contract in February 2026 after G League stints with the Bulls and Cavaliers organizations.
roster.name: Emanuel Miller

roster.facts: Re-signed on a one-year veteran minimum in 2026 as the emergency backup point guard behind Fox, Castle, and Harper.
roster.name: Jordan McLaughlin
